estimator.name: CE, the corrected-eigenvector convergent point: an errors-in-variables correction of the committed eigenvector estimator (the plain estimator and its legs are unchanged)
estimator.problem: design finding F4 of Part A: the plain convergent point is the smallest eigenvector of S = sum b_i b_i^T, b_i = n_i x t_i. A star whose observed proper-motion direction is rotated in the tangent plane by a small angle delta_i has b_i = b0_i cos(delta_i) - t_i sin(delta_i), b0_i perpendicular to the true convergent point c, so E[S] = sum (1 - E delta_i^2) b0_i b0_i^T + sum E delta_i^2 t_i t_i^T. The second sum is not perpendicular to c (t_i . c = sin theta_i) and pulls the smallest eigenvector towards the cluster, along the one direction the stars constrain weakly (their great circles are nearly parallel): the bias of +1.29 percent in pi_MC measured on the design stream of Part A.
estimator.noiseVariance: delta_i^2 = tau^2 / sin^2(theta_i) + s_i^2 / mu_i^2 (rad^2). First term: an isotropic internal velocity scatter sigma_int per axis rotates the observed direction of the tangential motion by sigma_int / (V sin theta_i), so the offsets b_i . c have the same intrinsic scatter tau = sigma_int / V (rad) for every star and the direction error is tau / sin theta_i. Second term: the measurement; s_i^2 = (b_i . e_i)^2 sigma_pmra,i^2 + (b_i . g_i)^2 sigma_pmdec,i^2 is the variance of the proper motion across the track (e_i east, g_i north; the correlation is zero, as committed), mu_i the observed proper-motion magnitude.
estimator.tau: estimated from the offsets alone (no radial velocity, no speed): over U, the members with sin theta_i >= 0.1 at the current c, n = |U| > 2: lambda = sum_U (b_i . c)^2; M_i = sin^2(theta_i) s_i^2 / mu_i^2 (the measurement part of the variance of b_i . c); tau^2 = max(0, (lambda n / (n - 2) - sum_U M_i) / n). The factor n / (n - 2) restores the two parameters the fit used. The 3-sigma clip of the membership iteration truncates the offsets and shrinks lambda by about 2.7 percent; that is not corrected and is a stated limit.
estimator.iteration: c_0 is the plain eigenvector of the stars of U_0 (members with sin theta >= 0.1 at the plain convergent point), signed so that sum t_i . u_i > 0. For k = 1, 2, ...: U_k is formed at c_{k-1}; tau^2 and delta_i^2 are computed at c_{k-1}; S*_k = sum_{U_k} b_i b_i^T - sum_{U_k} delta_i^2 t_i t_i^T; c_k is the eigenvector of the smallest eigenvalue of S*_k (a 3 by 3 symmetric eigenproblem), signed by the same rule. Stop when the angle between c_k and c_{k-1} is at most 1e-12 rad. 100 iterations without a stop: the CE estimate is not returned, the result is refused with the reason ce-no-convergence (no fallback to the plain estimate; a refused realization counts as not covering).
estimator.rest: the speed V (weighted least squares of the radial velocity on cos theta, committed), the per-star and cluster parallax (committed formulas, weights 1 / parallax_error^2) and every refusal (fewer than 20 members, sigma_off above 3 degrees, radial-velocity scatter above 3 km/s, fewer than 10 members with a radial velocity, perpendicular, sign, interval above 10 percent, more than 5 percent of replicates discarded) are those of Part A, evaluated at the CE convergent point and applied to the members the amended iteration found. The members are NOT reselected with CE inside the iteration (stated choice).
estimator.bootstrap: the members are resampled with replacement (member set fixed, as committed), CE is refitted in every replicate (tau^2 re-estimated from the replicate), the speed is refitted, pi_MC recomputed; B = 400 per synthetic realization, 4000 for the real sample; sigma_MC half the distance between the 15.865th and 84.135th percentiles; the 95.45 percent interval the 2.275th to 97.725th (as committed). A replicate whose CE does not converge, with a non-positive speed or fewer than 5 stars, is discarded; more than 5 percent discarded refuses (unstable).
estimator.inputs: the proper-motion errors: the file pmra_error and pmdec_error columns for the real sample; for synthetic stars both equal to the star parallax sigma (the committed syntheticTruth.errors.properMotionSigma). Correlations are zero (not columns of the file).
estimator.assumptions: stated, and the legs test the first two on worlds where they hold and E6 reports a world where the third fails: the internal velocity scatter is isotropic; the cluster shares one space velocity; there is no expansion or rotation (D5 and K15 report what the plain and corrected estimators do when there is). The correction is first order in delta^2 (delta below about 0.1 rad for sin theta >= 0.1).
estimator.whatItIsNot: no tuning constant, no knob: every quantity is read from the data or is a committed constant (the 0.1 floor on sin theta, 1e-12 rad, 100 iterations); not a maximum-likelihood fit (that is a different estimator and would be a new contract).

thresholdRule.rule: Every bound of a follow-up leg is fixed by the following rule, which was written before any follow-up number existed. (1) A leg that re-tests a committed leg takes that leg bound unchanged on an ensemble of the same size, so the committed arithmetic holds. The nominal levels of the intervals are 68.27 and 95.45 percent (one and two Gaussian standard deviations). The coverage band of the 68.27 percent interval is the nominal rate plus or minus three binomial standard errors at n = 200: 0.6827 +- 3 sqrt(0.6827 * 0.3173 / 200) = 0.584 to 0.781, committed as 0.58 to 0.78 (C3). The band of the 95.45 percent interval is the committed 0.90 to 0.99 (C4; the upper bound below 1 because a finite bootstrap cannot be asked to cover always). The bound on the median of z is three standard errors of a median of 200 unit normals, 3 * 1.2533 / sqrt(200) = 0.266, committed as 0.27 (C5); the bound on the median relative bias is the committed 0.005 (C5). The usefulness, agreement, convergent-point, no-radial-velocity, analytic, oracle and real-sample bounds are the committed C7, C6, C2, D2a and D2b, A1 to A3, B2, B3, B5, B6 and R1 to R5 bounds. (2) E7 and E8 have no committed analogue; each takes the four C3 to C5 bounds at the same n = 200. (3) No value is derived from a measured number of the failing legs C3, C4, C5 (coverage 0.495 and 0.885, median z +0.89, median relative bias +0.0117), or from any other result of Part A. (4) R7 and R8 use only committed constants (the 3 sigma factor, the 3 percent cap, sigma0 = 1.0 km/s, the synthetic positionSigma 5 pc) and the printed values of the published-value fixtures; their rules are written below and not changed after the real-sample CE run.
thresholdRule.disclosure: What the author of this follow-up had seen before writing this file, stated so the order can be judged: all of Part A (MOVING_CLUSTER_GATE.md and the fixtures, including the amended form real-sample convergent point at (97.11, 7.08) degrees, V of 46.3 km/s, the ratio 1.0146 to 233 pi_plx, and the synthetic bias of F4); and the published-value file Carl fetched (including the printed Perryman convergent point and distance). The R7 and R8 rules were not set from the gap between those; they are built from the committed constants named in (4). No CE number of any kind, on any seed or on the real file, existed when this file was committed.
thresholdRule.noPowerClaim: A band that cannot fail would be no test: K5 to K7 would have failed on the plain estimator of Part A (they are its C3 to C5, which failed) and a corrected estimator that carries the same bias fails them again.

publishedComparisons.sources: tests/fixtures/moving-cluster/published-cp.json and published-distance.json, transcribed from the PDFs Carl fetched (arXiv:astro-ph/9707253v1, sha256 924ec0c8...f670, and arXiv:1811.03845v1, sha256 64266b1d...68d8) as printed, checked line by line against the text extracted beside them. Untrusted data: read, not executed, nothing fetched by this session, no number typed from memory.
publishedComparisons.cpHasNoUncertainty: Perryman et al. print the convergent point, for 134 and for 180 stars, with no uncertainty. RK7 therefore has no published sigma: its tolerance is ours (3 r of the bootstrap) plus the stated floor f for the difference between two member selections. A pass says the two convergent points agree to within what the Hipparcos core and our larger Gaia sample may be expected to differ by; it is not a statement that the published value is exact.
publishedComparisons.distanceConcept: the published distance is to the centre of mass of the Hipparcos members within 10 pc (the paper says the concept is meaningful only in that restricted context); our pi_MC is a parallax-weighted mean over our members. The floor g pi_pub in RK8 is the stated allowance for that concept difference. The Gaia DR2 (47.50 +- 0.15 pc) and DR1 (46.75 +- 0.46 pc) values are second-hand quotations from the introduction of Roser et al. 2019, not primary sources, not the same estimand, and are REPORTED only (RK8r).
publishedComparisons.epoch: Perryman et al. use Hipparcos astrometry at epoch J1991.25; the sample is Gaia DR3 at J2016.0 (ICRS). The convergent point is a direction of the cluster space velocity and does not depend on the epoch; the two member sets differ.

gate.verdictFunction: the committed verdict function of thresholds.json applied to the follow-up rows alone: S legs are the follow-up legs with set S, R legs those with set R; A when every S and R follow-up leg passes; B when every geo leg of S and R passes and some dist leg fails or is NOT RUN; C when a geo leg fails or is NOT RUN. A REPORTED leg and a NOT RUN leg without a set are never in either set. It describes the corrected estimator on these legs; it does not change the committed verdict C (whose legs stay as recorded and are not re-measured), does not ratify AM1 to AM3, and authorizes no consumer, no Part B and no distance (consumersRule above).

findings: F5. The estimator behaves as specified. Relative bias of pi_MC against the weighted true parallax, plain then CE: field-free baseline +1.218 percent (se 0.087) then +0.008 (se 0.087); baseline in the field +1.140 (se 0.139) then -0.031 (se 0.138); internal sigma 1.0 km/s +4.972 (se 0.209) then +0.056 (se 0.202); convergent point 60 degrees away +1.199 (se 0.165) then -0.001 (se 0.164). The fixed point converged in 5 or 6 iterations on every realization that returned one; the estimated tau was 0.62 to 0.64 degrees for a true 0.637 (sigma_int 0.5 km/s over V 45) and 1.264 degrees for a true 1.273 (sigma_int 1.0). The median convergent-point error fell from 0.34 to 0.14 degrees (baseline) and from 1.34 to 0.24 degrees (internal sigma 1.0). These are design numbers on a design seed, not legs; no bound was read from them.

F6. The implementation reuses the amended membership iteration of Part A (the analyse function, unchanged), whose last step refuses on fewer than 20 members, sigma_off above 3 degrees or a radial-velocity scatter above 3 km/s evaluated at the plain convergent point, before CE exists. The estimator text says every refusal is evaluated at the CE point. Recorded as AM4.
